content.specificationName: Enable Hot-Reload for MCP Clients in Development Mode
content.purpose: Enable testing metabob-cli code changes without restarting opencode session by hot-reloading MCP client connections
content.summary: MCP clients are initialized once at startup via Instance.state() and never reconnected. Config reload exists but doesn't trigger MCP reconnection. Need to add MCP.reload() that closes/re-initializes clients and integrate with config reload system.

components.currentBehavior: Lines 153-188: state = Instance.state(async () => {...}) initializes MCP clients once on first access. The state function caches clients and only disposes them when Instance.dispose() is called. No reload/reconnect functionality exists.
components.desiredBehavior: Add MCP.reload() function that: (1) Calls await state() to get current clients, (2) Closes all existing clients gracefully, (3) Re-reads config via Config.get(), (4) Re-initializes clients using create() function, (5) Updates state with new clients, (6) Returns status per client
components.gap: No reload function exists. Need to add MCP.reload() that disposes old state and re-initializes

components.currentBehavior: Lines 217-357: create() function initializes a single MCP client (local or remote), connects transport, lists tools, returns client and status. Already handles connection failures gracefully.
components.desiredBehavior: No changes needed. This function already handles client initialization and can be reused for reload.

components.currentBehavior: Lines 177-187: Instance.state() dispose callback closes all clients when Instance.dispose() is called. This happens during full config reload.
components.desiredBehavior: MCP.reload() should have its own disposal logic that closes clients before re-initializing, without disposing the entire Instance state (which would clear ALL cached state).
components.gap: Need selective disposal of MCP clients only, not full Instance.dispose()

components.currentBehavior: Lines 63-95: reload() function checks safety, calls Instance.dispose() to invalidate all cached state. This disposes MCP clients but doesn't re-initialize them until next access.
components.desiredBehavior: After calling Instance.dispose(), should explicitly call MCP.reload() to ensure MCP clients are re-initialized immediately (not lazily on next access).
components.gap: Missing explicit MCP.reload() call after Instance.dispose()

components.currentBehavior: Lines 33-52: canReloadSafely() always returns true with TODO comments. No actual safety checks implemented.
components.desiredBehavior: Should check: (1) No active MCP tool calls in progress, (2) No running activities using MCP tools, (3) No open sub-sessions with MCP context. For MVP, existing behavior (always safe) is acceptable with manual reload trigger.
components.gap: Safety checks not implemented but not blocking for manual reload MVP

components.currentBehavior: Lines 84-96: analyzeKeyModification() detects MCP config changes and adds warnings about server restarts. Already identifies which MCP servers are affected.
components.desiredBehavior: No changes needed. Already provides the impact analysis needed.

components.currentBehavior: Lines 7-80: Only has 'mcp add' command for adding new MCP servers interactively. No reload command.
components.desiredBehavior: Add 'mcp reload' command that: (1) Checks if reload is safe, (2) Calls MCP.reload(), (3) Reports success/failure per client, (4) Shows updated client status.

components.currentBehavior: Lines 20-230: test_metabob_mcp tool tests Metabob MCP connectivity, lists tools, tests search_activities. Good for verifying reload worked.
components.desiredBehavior: No changes needed. Can be used to verify reload success. Consider adding generic MCP health check for all clients (not just Metabob).
components.gap: No generic health check, but existing tool is sufficient for testing

components.currentBehavior: Lines 32-100, 1227-1229: state = Instance.state(async () => {...}) loads all config once and caches. Config.get() returns cached state. Config.update() writes file and calls Instance.dispose().
components.desiredBehavior: No changes needed. MCP.reload() will call Config.get() to re-read config after Instance.dispose().

dataFlow.currentFlow: User edits opencode.json → Instance.state() cache remains stale → MCP clients use old config until full restart
dataFlow.desiredFlowManual: User edits opencode.json → User runs 'opencode mcp reload' → canReloadSafely() check → MCP.reload() closes old clients → Config.get() re-reads config → create() initializes new clients → Return status report
dataFlow.desiredFlowAutomatic: User edits opencode.json → config/reload.ts detects change → canReloadSafely() check → Instance.dispose() → MCP.reload() → New clients ready

implementationPlan.details: Export async function reload() that: (1) Gets current state, (2) Closes all existing clients, (3) Gets fresh config, (4) Re-initializes clients with create(), (5) Updates state, (6) Returns status per client
After Instance.dispose() on line 88, add: await MCP.reload() to ensure MCP clients are re-initialized immediately
Add McpReloadCommand to repos/metabob-opencode/packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/mcp.ts that calls MCP.reload() and displays results
Verify: (1) Change metabob-cli code, (2) Restart metabob-cli vessel, (3) Run 'opencode mcp reload', (4) Verify new tools/behavior active, (5) Check test_metabob_mcp tool shows updated state

currentStateDetails.mcpInitialization: MCP clients initialized lazily on first MCP.state() call via Instance.state() caching mechanism
currentStateDetails.configReload: Config reload exists with safety checks but only disposes state, doesn't explicitly reload MCP
currentStateDetails.clientLifecycle: Clients created once, disposed on Instance.dispose(), no reconnection logic
currentStateDetails.impactAnalysis: Already detects MCP config changes and warns about restarts
currentStateDetails.cliCommands: Only 'mcp add' exists, no reload command

desiredStateDetails.mcpReload: MCP.reload() function that gracefully closes and re-initializes clients with new config
desiredStateDetails.configIntegration: Config reload automatically triggers MCP.reload() when MCP config changes
desiredStateDetails.cliCommand: 'opencode mcp reload' command for manual reload during development
desiredStateDetails.safetyChecks: Prevent reload during active MCP operations (future enhancement, not MVP)
desiredStateDetails.logging: Detailed logs at each reload step for debugging

testScenario.setup: metabob-opencode running with metabob-cli as MCP vessel
testScenario.change: Modify metabob-cli code (e.g., add logging to search_activities tool)
testScenario.vessel: Restart metabob-cli vessel to pick up code changes
testScenario.reload: Run 'opencode mcp reload' or trigger config reload
testScenario.verify: Call metabob_search_activities tool and verify new logging appears
testScenario.alternative: Use test_metabob_mcp tool to verify connection and tools are updated

criticalInsights.instanceStatePattern: Instance.state() provides per-instance caching with lazy initialization and disposal lifecycle
criticalInsights.stateNotSubState: MCP state is managed by Instance.state(), not a simple variable - requires understanding the State pattern
criticalInsights.disposalVsReload: Instance.dispose() clears ALL state (config, MCP, tools). MCP.reload() should be selective.
criticalInsights.createIsReusable: The create() function (lines 217-357) is already well-structured for reuse in reload
criticalInsights.circuitBreaker: Circuit breaker state (lines 70) needs to be preserved or reset on reload - consider implications
